verdict.rationale: Maritime runs any Docker container you supply on its own micro-VM, so arbitrary code and packages can be baked in at build time. It also offers persistent Linux desktops that agents can drive. However, no documented exec or shell-command API, and no runtime package-install capability, appears in the evidence. missing for 10: a documented interface for running arbitrary shell commands inside a running sandbox, explicit runtime package installation, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run arbitrary shell commands and install packages inside the sandbox

citations.quote: Any Docker container becomes an agent: three endpoints get you sleep/wake, channels, and triggers.
Any repo with a Dockerfile can be served on a public, no-login HTTPS URL. Maritime builds it, runs it serverlessly
its own always-on micro-VM in the cloud, persistent storage
A persistent Linux desktop (XFCE, Chromium, LibreOffice) for each of _your_ end users, driven by _your_ model.
